sections.title: Prerequisite Review: From Discrete to Continuous
sections.content: Briefly recap discrete probability (bars). Transition to continuous variables where the probability of any exact point is zero, shifting the focus from 'height of a bar' to 'area under a curve'.
sections.example: Comparing a histogram of test scores (discrete bars) to a smooth bell curve representing the same data distribution.

sections.title: Defining the PDF
sections.content: Introduce the PDF as a function f(x) where the area under the curve between two points equals the probability. Emphasize two rules: f(x) ≥ 0 and total area = 1.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Probability Fluid' being poured into a container—the total volume (area) must always equal 1 (100% certainty).

sections.title: The Geometric Interpretation
sections.content: Explain that finding the probability of a range [a, b] is equivalent to calculating the integral (area) under the curve between those bounds.
sections.example: A robotic arm's precision: The PDF shows the likelihood of it landing in a specific 2cm zone; we calculate the shaded area to find the success rate.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Squirrel’s Acorn Search
sections.content: Synthesize the knowledge: A squirrel drops an acorn. The PDF shows where it lands. We use the area under the curve to predict the squirrel's most likely hunting zone.
sections.example: An animation showing a squirrel moving across an X-axis; the PDF curve spikes where the squirrel spends most of its time searching.

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
sections.content: Recap: The PDF is not a probability itself, but a density. Integration provides the probability. Total area must equal 1.
sections.example: A 'Cheat Sheet' graphic overlaying a curve with the equation ∫f(x)dx = 1, reinforcing the fundamental rule of total probability.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: From Discrete to Continuous
lecture_lines: Discrete probability uses bars for distinct outcomes.
Continuous variables mean zero probability at exact points.
Focus shifts from bar height to area under curves.

storyboard.title: Defining the PDF
lecture_lines: PDF defines probability through area under a curve.
Two rules: curve is positive and area is one.
Total area represents hundred percent certainty.
animations: Show area under curve filling with #33A1FF.

storyboard.title: The Geometric Interpretation
lecture_lines: Probabilities are integrals over a specific interval.
Area under the curve equals probability of range.
Use geometry to find likelihoods of specific zones.

storyboard.title: Real-World Application: The Squirrel’s Acorn Search
lecture_lines: PDF predicts outcomes like squirrel acorn drops.
Curve spikes show where events likely occur.
Area under spikes reveals hunting success zones.

storyboard.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
lecture_lines: PDF is a density, not a probability.
Integration calculates probability from density functions.
Total area must always equal one.
